To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

data provenance models are diverse, that there are many different approaches for data provenance, that there are no standard models or implementations for data provenance and that the requirements of different application domains have to be taken into account when designing provenance models.
there exist different types of data provenance, each of them with different properties and requirements.
data provenance models can be categorized according to the data model, data processing facilities, the provenance model, the provenance representation, and the application domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a better understanding of the concept of provenance and with the development of a generic provenance model that covers all kinds of data representation models, data processing facilities and application domains.
the question of how to represent and query provenance in a generic manner, i.e., independently from a specific application domain or data model.
the development of a comprehensive provenance model, which is able to cover a wide range of application domains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
data provenance is a research field that has been investigated from different perspectives, but still lacks a general and uniform approach.
data provenance is a very complex problem that requires further research in many different areas.
there is no single provenance model that can be applied in all application areas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the existing approaches are not well suited for the general case of provenance, but they provide a good foundation for the development of a generic provenance system.
there is no single solution for provenance that fits all requirements.
we need to distinguish between different data representation models and different data processing facilities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a number of open problems and challenges in the area of provenance.
the existing approaches are very domain specific and that there is a need for a more general approach.
the existing models of provenance are too limited and do not cover the needs of many application domains.
